builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DAC-Loop: Distillation-Aware Compression for Remote Sensing CNN
summary: The method replaces one-shot structured pruning plus a single KD recovery stage with an iterative loop that applies distillation before and after pruning and alternates structured pruning with unstructured sparsification. It costs extra training cycles, pruning-schedule tuning, and implementation complexity because unstructured sparsity does not automatically translate into wall-clock or energy gains unless the deployment stack supports it. It can fail when the target hardware only realizes dense structured speedups, when the teacher or fine-tuning data are unavailable, or when accuracy degrades on classes sensitive to aggressive compression.
rationale: The approach fits a 24 GB GPU and edge-oriented production goals, but its value depends on workload-specific validation of whether the claimed parameter reduction yields usable latency, memory, and accuracy benefits on the reader's hardware and data.
technique: Distillation-aware iterative pruning for edge CNNs

claims.statement: The method replaces one-shot structured pruning plus a single KD recovery stage with an iterative loop that applies distillation before and after pruning and alternates structured pruning with unstructured sparsification. It costs extra training cycles, pruning-schedule tuning, and implementation complexity because unstructured sparsity does not automatically translate into wall-clock or energy gains unless the deployment stack supports it. It can fail when the target hardware only realizes dense structured speedups, when the teacher or fine-tuning data are unavailable, or when accuracy degrades on classes sensitive to aggressive compression.

The paper reports that DAC-Loop improves the accuracy-compression trade-off and maintains strong accuracy beyond 90% parameter reduction, but the abstract provides no exact accuracy or compression factor for audit.
